title: Spillover containment and credit throttler for dedicated clusters
creator: Evelyn Zhang
description: Post-incident follow-up for the 2026-03-08 capacity storm where a noisy tenant exhausted KV-cache and request credits, causing spillover across adjacent reservations. Investigation identified reservation undersizing for burst patterns and an ineffective global burst tokenbucket that allowed cross-tenant credit transfer. This ticket scopes a two-part mitigation: (1) a containment mechanism that prevents spillover from a saturated reservation to neighbors, and (2) a 'credit throttler' microservice that enforces per-tenant soft-credit budgets with adaptive refill (split-burst) behavior.
steps_taken: 1) Emergency mitigations: temporarily reduced burst window on affected clusters; manually increased reservation for top noisy tenant; enabled conservative eviction thresholds. 2) Postmortem telemetry: collected per-tenant KV cache usage, eviction rates, tokenbucket drain curves and p95/p99 latency heatmaps. 3) Short spike fix: rolled out per-tenant soft-quota limiter to one region as a canary.
action_items: Design containment: define 'spillover' signals (cache evictions delta, sustained queue length, token drain rate) and containment thresholds — owner: Marcus Lee — due 2026-03-21
Implement credit-throttler prototype (Go service) with split-burst refill and tenant scoping; integrate with router for fast-path enforcement — owner: Priya Nair — estimate 5 — due 2026-04-04
Reservation autosizer rule: add burst-aware heuristic that inflates reservation for tenants with high prefix-reuse and wide tail latency — owner: Data Team (assigned lead: Omar Ruiz) — due 2026-04-11
Dashboard and alerts: add 'spillover index' metric, set SLO-alarm and runbook link; create runbook steps for containment activation — owner: SRE Team (lead: Linh Tran) — due 2026-03-25
Canary and rollout plan: deploy credit-throttler in one Dedicated cluster, monitor fairness and latency regressions for two weeks, then stagger global rollout — owner: Marcus Lee — due 2026-04-18
E2E tests: synthetic multi-tenant workload that simulates cache-saturated spillover and validates that containment preserves neighbor P95 — owner: QA — estimate 3 — due 2026-04-01
acceptance_criteria: Containment triggers when spillover index > 0.8 and reduces cross-reservation token transfer by >= 90% in canary clusters
Credit-throttler maintains p95 latency within 10% of baseline for steady workloads while preventing neighbor degradation under burst tests
Autosizer rule suggests reservation increase for identified tenants with >3x burst-to-baseline ratio with actionable recommendation in Console
Runbook exists and on-call can activate containment manually within 3 minutes; alerts validated via chaos tests
resolution_summary: Goal is to eliminate cascading neighbor impact from single-tenant behavior by adding explicit isolation controls (containment) and predictable, tunable per-tenant soft-credits (credit-throttler). Deliverables: production-ready throttler, autosizing heuristic, dashboards/alerts, and validated rollout.
notes: This approach prefers graceful degradation of the noisy tenant rather than hard ejection to reduce customer impact.
Design should allow policy overrides for enterprise customers with reserved contracts.
Consider future work: per-model KV cache partitioning and per-instance burst tokens.
